newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Former Mobutu ally detained briefly in New Congo.
newsitem.headline: Former Mobutu ally detained briefly in New Congo.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila's government held a former associate of ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko overnight as part of an embezzlement inquiry, according to family members and his bodyguard.
Businessman Bemba Saolona was arrested on Thursday and then released on Friday, his bodyguard told Reuters.
Family members said on Friday that Bemba was taken away from his house by a group of soldiers with an arrest warrant.
"They said he would be held some time for questioning. They have accused him of embezzling public money," his wife said.
"I hope justice will be done, to establish that he is not guilty. Apparently they say he misused funds belonging to the national airline but he was not the boss of Air Zaire."
The bodyguard said that Bemba had been confronted with the former managing director of Air Zaire, General Kikunda Ombala.
Kabila came to power in May, ending 32 years of Mobutu rule after a seven-month guerrilla war.
Bemba was president of the national business association and a member of the transitional legislature Kabila has dissolved. He advocated negotiations with Kabila early in the revolt.
Mobutu, who is sick with cancer and in exile, and cronies reputedly embezzled billions of dollars. More than 30 dignitaries of the Mobutu regime are currently in detention.

The government has pledged to freeze foreign bank accounts as part of efforts to return embezzled money to the former Zaire, renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo by Kabila. The government says it has inherited empty state coffers.
